reviewer: /root main coordinator; bounded source-level cross-layer comparison; no runtime execution
title: Employee compensation input validation across cashier UI and server/payroll
scope: Compare employee compensation form validation with create/update handlers, employee-ledger credit paths and payroll aggregation. This supplements the existing compensation-mode casing comparison (SEM-MIRROR-008) and unpromoted employee-credit admission leads; it is not the same issue.
decision: CASHIER FORM REJECTS NEGATIVE PROFILE MONEY VALUES, BUT SERVER CREATE/UPDATE COPY SIGNED VALUES WITHOUT A SERVER-SIDE AMOUNT GUARD; DOWNSTREAM ATTENDANCE AND LEDGER HANDLERS CAN STORE NEGATIVE CREDIT FACTS. SOURCE-CONFIRMED VALIDATION DIVERGENCE; FINANCIAL LOSS/SETTLEMENT CONSEQUENCE AND ZERO/NEGATIVE BUSINESS POLICY REQUIRE TESTS/OWNER CONTRACT. NO RUNTIME INCIDENT CLAIMED.

behavior.client: EmployeeEditorViewModel.CreateRequest rejects negative daily/shift amounts; TryOptionalMoney does the same for optional monthly/overtime values. It accepts zero and sends typed create/update DTOs.
behavior.server: CreateEmployeeHandler and UpdateEmployeeHandler call EmployeeRules.AssertEmployeeInput (identity fields only), parse CompensationType and authorize employees_manage, then assign signed numeric request values to EmployeeEntity without amount constraints. Route handlers forward DTOs to these services.
behavior.downstream: RecordDailyWage/Overtime/ExtraShift handlers post earning values as ledger credits. BiometricCheckInHandler posts stored DailyWage for Daily compensation without a positive guard. EmployeeLedgerPoster stores signed debit/credit fields as passed. PayrollRules sums those credits into buckets and floors only final NetPayable at zero.
behavior.interpretation: This is an actual client/server validation difference, not an authorization bypass: profile commands remain permission-gated. A privileged non-UI caller can persist negative compensation values and subsequent earning flows can create negative credit facts. Whether those requests should be rejected is a financial invariant strongly implied by wage/rate semantics but needs explicit owner/domain contract; no actual API or database call was executed.

cross_file_call_chain: EmployeeEditorViewModel.CreateRequest -> Create/UpdateEmployeeRequest signed long fields -> Program.cs employee POST/PUT -> CreateEmployeeHandler/UpdateEmployeeHandler -> EmployeeEntity signed bigint fields.

Persisted DailyWage -> BiometricCheckInHandler or RecordDailyWageHandler -> EmployeeLedgerPoster credit column -> CreatePayrollHandler/PayrollRules.CalculatePayrollLines -> payroll line net/pay eligibility.
RecordOvertimeHandler and RecordExtraShiftHandler -> EmployeeLedgerPoster -> payroll overtime/extra-shift credit sums.

existing_evidence.candidate_disposition: Do not create a duplicate canonical finding before Financial Integrity agent challenges this cross-layer evidence and owner policy is distinguished from source behavior.

counterevidence_and_limits: The normal Cashier WinUI employee form blocks negative compensation values.
Create/update server methods require employees_manage authorization; no permission bypass is asserted.
Zero amounts are accepted intentionally/possibly for some compensation arrangements; recommendation must preserve legitimate zero/null semantics unless owner decides otherwise.
Source proves signed values flow through the path, not that a user entered them, a payroll was paid, or real money was lost.
UI edit and API request tests, SQL persistence and payroll settlement were not executed. Existing integration tests reviewed cover valid paths only in cited span.
recommendation: Future repair should enforce shared server/domain constraints for each compensation amount at create/update and for custom wage/rate entry points, while preserving optional null and legitimate zero values per owner policy. Add one invariant source of truth; keep client validation for UX but do not rely on it. Confirm hourly/monthly/daily/shift business semantics before deciding which fields may be zero. Do not conflate profile-input validation with the separate payroll adjustment historical-rate policy.

needed: Create and update employee requests with negative DailyWagePiastres, ShiftValuePiastres, MonthlySalaryPiastres and OvertimeRatePiastres are rejected server-side; zero/null cases remain accepted or rejected according to an explicit policy.
Direct daily-wage request with negative CustomWagePiastres and stored negative wage is rejected or otherwise reconciled by stated contract.

Direct overtime request tests negative CustomRatePiastres, zero rate, nonfinite Hours at pure handler boundary, finite extreme Hours and multiplication/long conversion bounds; HTTP JSON binder behavior separately.
ExtraShift with negative/zero ShiftValue fallback to negative/zero DailyWage and large ShiftCount tests arithmetic boundary.
Biometric check-in with zero/negative persisted daily wage must not produce invalid negative credit if policy prohibits it; verify duplicate/idempotency behavior.
Payroll calculation with negative DailyWage/Overtime/ExtraShift credit records has explicit handling; assert base/net/report totals and inactive employee behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Server and UI agree on the domain-approved compensation constraints.
No path stores a negative earning credit if negative wages/rates are disallowed.
Valid zero, nullable salary and legacy employee profiles retain documented behavior.
Tests establish the impact on payroll lines and payment eligibility without posting real funds.

limitations: Bounded comparison of employee profile and wage-credit path; not an exhaustive mirror scan or proof of all client/server semantic parity.
Static source only; no tests, HTTP requests, database writes or payroll settlement executed.
Severity and intended zero/negative input policy require Financial Integrity/owner disposition.

source_references.evidence: CreateRequest rejects negative daily/shift amounts and TryOptionalMoney rejects negative monthly/overtime amounts before building CreateEmployeeRequest/UpdateEmployeeRequest. Zero remains accepted; persisted form values are loaded back into the editor.
Create/update validate name, employee number, title, phone, compensation enum and employees_manage authorization, but copy signed compensation numeric fields without value checks.
AssertEmployeeInput validates only name/employee-number/job-title/phone; no compensation amount invariant.
Create/update DTO monetary properties are signed Int64 values (nullable monthly/overtime); no validation attributes or constructor guards.

Daily wage accepts custom-or-stored signed amount; overtime accepts signed custom rate and computes rounded rate*hours; extra shift falls back to daily wage when ShiftValue is not positive. Each posts a credit through EmployeeLedgerPoster; same-key replay semantics differ: daily wage throws on existing deterministic key while overtime/extra return existing row.

relevant_symbols.signature: Falah.Infrastructure.Employees.EmployeeLedgerPoster.PostIfNewAsync(Falah.Infrastructure.Persistence.FalahDbContext, string, string, string, string, Falah.Domain.Common.Money, Falah.Domain.Common.Money, string, string?, string?, string?, double?, long?, long?, CancellationToken)

source_references.evidence: Poster computes cached balance and stores passed debit/credit piastres as-is; it has no sign invariant or transaction/anchor lock in this helper.

Biometric check-in creates DailyWage credit directly for CompensationType Daily from stored DailyWagePiastres without positive guard; this is an alternate production path to the manual daily-wage command.

Payroll sums all DailyWage/Salary credits into base and Overtime/ExtraShift credits into their buckets; final net is floored at zero, but source ledger is not normalized/rejected for negative credits.

Typed create/update and wage endpoints forward requests to handlers. Handler-level employees_manage authorization governs profile writes; route is not a substitute for server-side monetary invariant validation.

Inspected test span covers ordinary valid wage/overtime/extra-shift and permission/dedup paths; it does not cover negative profile/custom amounts, negative overtime rate, nonfinite/extreme hours, or negative fallback wage. Tests were not executed.
